identity.title: TabStruct: Measuring Structural Fidelity of Tabular Data

problem.claim: Evaluate tabular data generators when heterogeneous data’s causal structure is difficult to inspect intuitively.

gap.claim: Existing benchmarks do not jointly analyze structural fidelity with conventional dimensions and often rely on toy datasets because ground-truth causal structures are rarely available for real-world data.

contributions.claim: A proposed evaluation framework jointly considers structural fidelity and conventional evaluation dimensions.
Global utility is introduced to assess structural fidelity without ground-truth causal structures.
TabStruct provides quantitative analysis of 13 tabular generators across nine categories and 29 datasets, with released datasets, pipelines, and raw results.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe their evaluation framework as novel and distinguish global utility as enabling structural-fidelity assessment without ground-truth causal structures.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that global utility offers a task-independent, domain-agnostic lens for tabular-generator performance.
The authors report large-scale quantitative analysis covering 13 generators, nine categories, and 29 datasets.
The authors report releasing the benchmark suite, including datasets, evaluation pipelines, and raw results.

narrative_sequence.summary: Tabular-generator evaluation is difficult because causal structure in heterogeneous data is not readily human-inspectable.
Structural fidelity has emerged as a tabular-specific evaluation dimension tied to real-data causal structure.
Existing benchmarks overlook interactions with conventional dimensions and are often restricted to toy datasets by missing causal ground truth.
The paper proposes joint evaluation and introduces global utility for settings without causal ground truth.
TabStruct evaluates generators across 29 datasets and releases the supporting benchmark materials.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs a newly defined metric with an explicit statement of the unavailable prerequisite it is intended to avoid: ground-truth causal structures.

lessons.interpretation: A method’s motivation becomes more testable when the proposed mechanism is directly linked to a concrete deployment constraint.
lessons.application: When presenting a new evaluation metric, state the missing or costly prerequisite it addresses and specify the scope in which it is intended to operate.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the prerequisite is actually available and central to the metric’s intended definition.

unknowns: The abstract does not report numerical results, baselines, statistical tests, or dataset composition beyond the stated counts.
It does not define how global utility is computed or establish whether the claimed lens improves evaluation decisions.
The abstract does not provide details permitting independent assessment of the framework’s or metric’s validity.
